meta.description: Create, revise, audit, and export submission-grade scientific figures for Nature-family and other high-impact venues in Python (matplotlib/seaborn) or R (ggplot2/patchwork/ComplexHeatmap), including multi-panel plots and journal-ready SVG/PDF/TIFF outputs. Supports AI-generated graphical abstracts via OpenRouter GPT Image 2. Enforces figure contract (core conclusion, evidence chain, archetype, backend exclusivity, journal export requirements) before plotting.

scientific_integrity.detail: Data-integrity gate enforces using all observations unless justified exclusion. Never reduces data merely for rendering convenience. Records before/after counts for any exclusions. Collision audit (audit_figure_collisions.py) mandatory after every change.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for scientific figure creation. Chart serves scientific logic, not aesthetics. Five-point contract (conclusion, evidence chain, archetype, backend, journal requirements) ensures defensible figures. AI-generated schematics treated as drafts with human verification requirement.

methodological_ground.detail: Multi-panel evidence architecture follows sound principles: one Results-level question per figure, complementary panel roles, paired differences for matched data. Backend exclusivity prevents visual inconsistency. QA contract includes rendered collision audit.

code_usability.detail: Backend preference script (nature_figure_backend.py) for persistence. Validation tools (validate_figure.py, audit_pdf_text.py, audit_figure_collisions.py) provided. Python CSV templates in template-catalog.md. R workflow documented.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive figure workflow: planning (contract, evidence architecture), generation (Python/R backends), revision, audit (collision/text/visual QA), export (SVG/PDF/TIFF). AI-generated graphical abstract route separate. Journal-specific requirements (Nature flagship, NMI). Template adaptation guidance.

reliability.note: Excellent quality gates: data-integrity gate prevents silent data reduction, backend exclusivity prevents cross-rendering inconsistency, collision audit mandatory after every change, 5pt font floor enforced, missing runtime check before rendering. QA contract includes panel-by-panel visual inspection.

performance_context.note: Efficient static/dynamic split: only selected backend fragment loaded (not both Python and R). On-demand references (2,600+ lines) loaded only when needed. Backend preference persistence prevents repeated asking.

agent_usability.note: Excellent routing protocol: clear 5-step process with backend gate, AI-schematic route separate from plotting. Five-point contract before plotting enforces structure. Backend preference script elegant. Manifest-driven fragment loading. References on-demand with clear conditions.

human_usability.note: Strong bilingual support (论文配图, 科研绘图). Backend preference remembered ('I will remember this as your default'). Tutorials and demos provided. Real Nature page archetypes (nature-2026-observations.md). Clear separation of AI-schematic vs data-plotting routes.

security.note: Privacy rule in core layer. No credential handling. Backend exclusivity prevents accidental data exposure through cross-rendering. Asset adaptation guidance for reusing templates without exposing source paths. AI-schematic route includes disclosure boundary and provenance requirements.

maintainability.note: Excellent modular architecture: core contract/stance, backend fragments, on-demand references. Backend preference persistence via external script (nature_figure_backend.py). Journal-specific requirements cleanly isolated. Version 2.7.1 shows active maintenance. Clear extension points.

agent_specific.note: Strong contract-driven workflow: five-point contract before code prevents premature implementation. Backend exclusivity principle excellent. Collision audit integration mandatory. Multi-panel evidence architecture sophisticated. Minor: lacks explicit guidance for chaining with nature-statistics for generating input data tables.

key_strengths: Exceptional contract-driven workflow: five-point contract (conclusion, evidence chain, archetype, backend, journal requirements) enforced before code prevents premature implementation
Excellent backend exclusivity principle: no cross-rendering between Python and R ensures visual consistency and prevents accidental data exposure
Strong data integrity: mandatory use of all observations unless justified, before/after counts recorded, unmodified source preserved
Robust quality assurance: collision audit (audit_figure_collisions.py) mandatory after every change, panel-by-panel visual inspection, 5pt font floor enforced
Clean separation of concerns: AI-generated schematics (OpenRouter route) separate from data plotting with human verification and provenance requirements

recommendations.title: Add graceful preference switch option when runtime missing
recommendations.problem: When selected backend runtime unavailable (e.g., R not installed), skill correctly stops and reports blocker but doesn't offer to switch backend preference if user wants to proceed immediately with available runtime (Python).
recommendations.root_cause: Missing runtime rule focuses on not falling back automatically (correct) but lacks user-initiated preference switch workflow for this scenario.
recommendations.fix: After reporting missing runtime blocker and installation commands, add: 'Alternatively, I can switch your saved preference to [other_backend] if you want to proceed now. This will become your new default. Would you like to: (1) install [selected] and continue, (2) switch to [other], or (3) stop?' Update nature_figure_backend.py to support switch confirmation.

recommendations.title: Add explicit production requirements pre-check before collision audit
recommendations.problem: For Nature flagship production figures, collision audit runs on PDF but doesn't explicitly validate 300 dpi and 180mm width requirements before audit. These are blocking requirements that should fail early.
recommendations.root_cause: Collision audit focuses on geometric collisions. Resolution and dimension checks implicit in journal requirements but not enforced systematically.
recommendations.fix: Add scripts/validate_production_requirements.py that checks: (1) PDF resolution ≥300 dpi, (2) figure width matches journal spec (180mm for Nature), (3) editable text present, (4) fonts embedded. Run before collision audit in QA contract workflow. Report blocking failures with remediation steps (re-export with correct dpi, resize canvas).

recommendations.title: Add integration guidance for nature-statistics skill
recommendations.problem: Figures often need input data tables generated from statistical analysis (summary stats, effect sizes, p-values). No explicit guidance for chaining with nature-statistics skill to generate these tables before plotting.
recommendations.root_cause: nature-figure focuses on visualization. Data preparation assumed to be user-provided or done externally. Cross-skill workflow not documented.
recommendations.fix: Add references/data-preparation-workflow.md documenting: (1) when to use nature-statistics before nature-figure, (2) expected output format from statistics (CSV/TSV schema), (3) validation checks (complete cases, numeric types, no NaN in critical columns), (4) example workflow: statistics → data validation → figure contract → plotting. Reference from figure-contract.md in evidence chain step.
